ai.description: *Dasia nicobarensis* is a medium-sized skink reaching 15 cm. It features a bronze-brown body with dark transverse bands and a pale underside. Key traits include a prehensile tail and arboreal habits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dasia nicobarensis* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of distinct, dark-edged pale transverse bands, which contrasts with the uniform or spotted backs of other Indian *Dasia* species.
ai.habitat: *Dasia nicobarensis* inhabits the tropical rainforests of the Nicobar Islands, typically dwelling in the canopy of tall trees within moist, evergreen forest ecosystems.
ai.behavior: The Nicobarese tree skink is primarily diurnal and arboreal, often seen basking on tree trunks or foraging for insects among the canopy foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dasia nicobarensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dasia nicobarensis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands, an archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, where it inhabits tropical forest environments at low elevations.
